Do you think someone who is struggling and in severe pain should have to the right to death, even if that means jeopardizing the happiness of others?

Edit: There are two sides to "pain". What's you opinion on mental illness related suicide and/or physical illness related suicide?
[Serious] Is suicide selfish? Should people have the right to death?
If all avenues for help have been exhausted and the person has given significant thought to this decision, I would consider it selfish to expect them to continue their existence to spare my feelings.
I don't think so. It's wrong to kill anyone, even yourself.
Correct me if I wrong, but wasn't giving your opinion the point of this thread. Should I say something else more popular and pretend like it is my opinion?

I don't think it's selfish at all. At the very end of my dad's life, after most of his cancer treatments had failed, he had the option for one more chemo treatment. This one had a very small chance of succeeding, but it would be devastating to his mind and body. He didn't really want to do it, but family convinced him. He had to suffer and die slowly; losing all real physical ability and sense of self. If anyone was selfish, it was those of us who wanted him to do whatever could possible save him no matter the probability.

If the time ever comes and I face the same options, I will choose the dignified death.

It's selfish, but then again, being selfish isn't actually bad in of itself as long as it's not harming other people. Even then, as long as you make sure to the best of your ability to make arrangements for your loved ones to be cared for after your death, there really isn't a problem with it in my opinion.

I feel like people should have the right to end their lives if they really feel like there isn't any reason to live, but we should at least give every person the resources they need to determine whether it's the right choice for them or not.

The issues is fishy. A person doesn't necessarily kill themselves because of depression. Don't remember who made the analogy, but it's like comparing a burning building and a trapped individual with a window as a means of escape.

Depression is similar to fire in this case, as it gets more intense and unbearable two things can happen. Be burned alive, or jump in an attempt to escape. Which of the options seem more appealing? Most would say jumping. Being burned alive is one of the worst ways to die possible. Depression could somewhat compare. The emotional struggle and distress gets so intense that they see no means of an escape. They decide to meet the lesser of the two fates - jumping, or in this case suicide.

Family members may not understand the circumstances, but they're not something that can be shrugged off and moving on with your life. I don't condone suicide by any means, but it should be an available option after all other ways of seeking help are exhausted.

In my opinion, yes it is selfish, but that does not necessarily mean it is a bad thing in any way. Suicide will have an affect on the people around you, but so will many other choices you make in life. In the same way that you have the right to leave a abusive relationship with the sole purpose of self preservation, you have the right to commit suicide. One thing that is definitely selfish in the way that I believe you mean in the question, i.e. Thoughtless and needlessly harmful to others, is the method of suicide which is the biggest point of contention for me. If you kill yourself by jumping in front of a crowded and publicly used train, damn right you are a fucking ass hole because you just traumatised countless people and possibly fucked up an expensive train system. If you are going to kill yourself, due to the nature of it being a selfish act, although you have all the right to do it, it is the least dick-ish if you do it in the most discrete way possible and not in front of anyone.
Interesting thoughts. I agree with the public suicide thing, if you're gonna do it, make it as painless as possible for you and others.
No one with a clear mind and a good perspective kills themselves. Just saying.

A teacher once said, "If you only remember one thing from my class, make it this: Suicide is a permanent solution to a temporary problem." Sure enough, I remember very little else from him, but that is sound advice. There are very few things that could be seen as a permanent problem without any possible solution. You can't predict what tomorrow will bring. Even if you are miserable, depressed and have no hope, try to find the smallest thing worth living for to get you through the day. Then repeat that each day until you find something larger to strive for.

To die with potential left to you? Yes it is selfish, but it is also a personal choice and one that only you should be allowed to make with whatever outside influence you yourself allow. Death with no other option but to suffer and fade into inhumanity is not selfish at all but noble, and should be treated as such.

Death when you yourself have since gone on to whatever you dream is afterwards and your family and loved ones have to make your choice for you is a kindness, to let a person go on when the light has left their eyes is the most profane cruelty a human can inflict upon another.

Suicide should be used as a means to end suffering of a terminal patient. Those afflicted by mental illness however, should seek treatment first, as the desire for suicide may be the result of them not thinking clearly.

If done for small reasons, especially those that aren't end of the life type suffering, I do consider it selfish. People shouldn't have the "right" to simple throw away everything over a whim, especially considering that society has taken care of them for so long.

I think that society views assisted suicide because of a physical ailment too differently. Just because I can't see their pain doesn't make it any less valid. However, assisted suicide people get the chance to say goodbye without as much judgement. Most mental illness related suicide, they can only leave a note because they don't have the freedom to make their peace. Which is sad to me.

Well Camus says suicide is the ultimate philosophical question. Which is no use here, but that made me sound clever, which is nice.

I think the very definition of suicide is selfishness, since it is the decision and act of killing oneself. That's when these "other people" step in, deciding for you that it is not reasonable to kill yourself against your will. From a society point of view, there is no alternative than : forbid suicide no matter what, respect suicide right no matter the condition (physical OR psychological), or check case by case in a legal and moral reflexion that may be too long for the issue.
